research.input: these three plates, the Swiss layer list, and whatever region the campaign already uses.
research.output: a density bible, not a map. Walk the real coast once and list what plate one bothers to name — peak, height, homestead, reserve, river fork, coast road — and what plates two and three delete. Do the same for a city quarter in Azlen’s grain: block, park void, arterial, fog wash, contour hill. Pull the Swiss stack across and rename the layers in fiction: old survey, every structure, coach posts, blazed paths, range days, closures.
research.done_when: you can point at a blank hex and say which six things must appear on it before it is allowed to be empty.
research.note_coach_posts: 'coach posts' is anachronistic: rename caravan halts / waystations

blank_hex.unit: the atlas has no hex grid; unit = one z7 tile (32 atlas px; a z5 tile is 128 px) or one league at a stated px scale (scale bar is Cyrikon-miles, scale unchecked)
blank_hex.not: the plate-one six, which include a shielded town that cannot be on every hex

planning.input: the density bible and the region.
planning.output: a sheet spec. Pick one coast, one river town, one painted city. Set label ranks: peaks and heights always, homesteads as dots, reserves as a green wash, only the river town gets a shield. Decide the Azlen rule for the city: texture over type, fog as weather not as art. Lock the overlay order so the 1864 sheet sits under the live one, and closures and range notices sit on top and can be swapped between sessions. Name the palette: bone paper, rust coast road, ocher arterials, rose-brown blocks, wet-blue water.
planning.done_when: a cartographer who has not seen the posts could draw sheet one from the spec alone.

implementation.output: the table map. Draw relief first, contours tight enough to read as fingerprints, then water, then the rust coast road, then green reserves, then homestead dots, then names and heights, then the city grain and fog washes last. Build the overlays as separate sheets: old survey, structures, coach posts, blazed paths, range days, closures. Do not generalize a ridge to save ink. If a knoll has no name, invent one. The crime in plates two and three is omission.
implementation.done_when: you can cover the settlement with a hand and still navigate by ridge names.
implementation.note: relief/contours/heights baked from EPESHU_HF (see pane_table for paint order); invented names deterministic via Patrinaic roots tool + tools/build-gazetteer.js

review.input: the finished sheet plus the three plates and the Swiss layer list.
review.output: a punch list. Check density against plate one, not against a normal virtual-tabletop map. Check the city against Azlen: does it look painted, or like a UI. Check the stack: can you pull the 1864 sheet, the closures, and the range notice without redrawing. Read every name aloud. Anything you cannot say at the table gets cut or rewritten. Mark the holes where you flinched and generalized.
review.done_when: the sparse version of your own map makes you angry.
review.sparse_version: produce it as a side-by-side at the same view: today's tiers against the new sheet (e.g. via the prototypes/atlas-night.html split). Otherwise 'makes you angry' cannot be checked.
